hints: Interpret each complex-number condition as a locus or region on the Argand diagram.
The condition $|z+2-3i|\leq2$ is the closed disc with centre $(-2,3)$ and radius $2$.
Draw the argument boundary ray from the origin at angle $3\pi/4$, decide which side satisfies $\arg z\leq3\pi/4$, and shade only its intersection with the disc; include both boundaries.
walkthrough:
Interpret the modulus condition $|z + 2 - 3\mathrm{i}| \leq 2$ by writing it in the standard distance form $|z - z_0| \leq r$:
$$|z - (-2 + 3\mathrm{i})| \leq 2$$
This represents a circle and its interior (a closed circular disc) with centre $C$ at $(-2, 3)$ and radius $r = 2$.

Identify key boundary points and tangent features of this circular disc:
Since the centre is at $x = -2$ and the radius is $r = 2$, the rightmost point of the circle is at $(-2 + 2, 3) = (0, 3)$, which means the circle touches the imaginary axis ($y$-axis) tangentially at $(0, 3)$.
The vertical span of the disc is from $y = 3 - 2 = 1$ to $y = 3 + 2 = 5$, and the horizontal span is from $x = -2 - 2 = -4$ to $x = 0$. Hence the circle lies entirely in the second quadrant.

Interpret the argument condition $\arg z \leq \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$:
The boundary $\arg z = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is a half-line (ray) radiating from the origin $O(0, 0)$ into the second quadrant, making an angle of $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ radians ($135^\circ$) with the positive real axis.
Along this ray, the coordinates satisfy $y = -x$ for $x < 0$.
The inequality $\arg z \leq \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ corresponds to all points whose argument is less than or equal to $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ (the region clockwise from the ray $\arg z = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$).

Determine how the ray intersects or relates to the circular disc:
Along the ray $y = -x$, when $x = -2$, we have $y = 2$.
The centre of the disc is at $(-2, 3)$, which has $y = 3 > 2$. Thus the point $(-2, 2)$ lies on the ray and is at distance $|3 - 2| = 1 < 2$ from the centre, meaning the ray passes through the interior of the disc.

Sketch the loci and shade the required intersection:
Draw a solid circle with centre at $(-2, 3)$ and radius $2$, tangent to the imaginary axis at $(0, 3)$.
Draw a solid ray starting from the origin at an angle of $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ ($135^\circ$) to the positive real axis.
Shade the region of points lying inside or on the boundary of the circle that are also on or clockwise from the half-line $\arg z = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.
